Create a polished publication-quality landscape architecture infographic, 16:9 wide composition at high resolution, with crisp legible text, generous spacing and meticulous aligned layout. White background, navy headings, cobalt blue outlines and arrows, orange accents for physical simulation, green for deterministic checks and records, purple for AI. Thin schematic line icons, clean professional engineering diagram style similar to a detailed hackathon winning project architecture poster. No photorealism, no decorative 3D, no invented cloud service logos. NanoForensics is the only product branding. Use exact scientifically honest labels specified below. Keep all text highly readable, avoid excessively tiny annotations. IMAGE 2 TITLE "NanoForensics — Technical Architecture" subtitle "Local full-stack workbench with isolated scientific records". Four well-spaced columns, with the middle runtime section larger. Use clean diagram connectors with labels and no crossings through text.
LEFT COLUMN header "RESEARCHER": desktop monitor with restrained generic dashboard, labels "Browser", "Next.js + React + TypeScript", "Inspect · investigate · results · evidence". Lower small terminal graphic "Read-only execution console / Search · JSON · export / Word reveal is a display effect". Arrow from browser to API labeled "HTTP requests & job polling"; separate dashed arrow return "Confirmed events & state". NO WebSocket or SSE labels.
CENTRAL LARGE BOUNDARY header "LOCAL APPLICATION RUNTIME". Upper blue block "Next.js frontend" and below navy "FastAPI backend". Inside FastAPI three tidy route rows "/api — original benchmark", "/api/demonstrations — published study", "/api/live-muse — AI rehearsal". Below "Durable job supervisor" with small labels "Per-case lock · deadlines · cancellation". A downward arrow "Isolated worker processes" leads into lower orange block "Registered scientific tools". In this block split "LAMMPS runtime" and "Vectorized NumPy fallback" under "2D shifted-force Lennard-Jones MD". Add "Measured stress–strain · trajectories · numerical diagnostics". Beside engine a green block "Independent evidence verifier" labels "Matched-seed comparison / Numerical checks / Supported · rejected · inconclusive". Arrow physics to verifier "Measured evidence". Arrow verifier back to supervisor "Verified results".
UPPER MIDDLE-RIGHT purple boundary "AI REASONING". Purple block "Meta Muse Spark API" with tiny cloud icon, not Google branding; labels "OpenAI-compatible structured JSON / Hypotheses · planning · evidence revision". Local adjacent amber block "Deterministic offline fallback / Explicit per-action provenance". Two-way arrows API backend↔AI labeled "Validated structured requests / Responses & action receipts". AI must not directly connect to or control a shell or solver. Small note "Registered tools only; no arbitrary execution".
RIGHT COLUMN blue header "ISOLATED DATA & AUDIT". Three separated cylinder database icons and labels "Original benchmark DB", "Published study DB", "AI rehearsal DB"; each labeled "SQLite". Smaller caption "Specimens · immutable results / Mutable state · durable jobs · events". Beneath databases green file box "Frozen scientific evidence / Public reports · protocol/source hashes / Published study: NOT_VALIDATED". Below dark outline box "Execution provenance / Actual engine · fresh or cached / Live API or visible fallback".
Connect backend↔databases labeled "Persist / restore", verifier→records "Evidence & verdicts". Avoid implying published results are modified by AI rehearsal.
BOTTOM LEGEND: solid navy arrow "Request / data", dashed blue arrow "Polling / events", purple arrow "Structured model calls"; footer "Implemented local architecture · Cloud hosting is not assumed". No Google Cloud, Firestore, Vertex AI, Pub/Sub, external telemetry hardware, Kubernetes, or fictional services. No invented numerical outcomes.
